messages:
maria: Heads-up — noticed a regression on KV route reuse after the recent kernel selector tweak (rolled ~1978620). TL;DR: /chat/stream kv hit-rate down from ~72% -> ~54% over the last 6h, evictions up ~2x, memory footprint steady. Posting quick traces + queries for triage.

perf-bot: alert: KV_CACHE_HITRATE_DROP on /chat/stream (72% -> 54%) — incident id: kv-197864 :rotating_light:

tyler: hmm. Did the rollout bump a quantized kernel or change padding/seq_len behavior? Any obvious change to batching heuristics?

maria: kernel selector change favored `aten_v2` over `cuda_fused` for small-seq cases. Batching config wasn't touched. Collected p50/p95/p99 token-latency slices + kv mem stats.

maria: prometheus queries I ran (raw):
```
avg_over_time(kv_cache_hitrate{route=\"/chat/stream\"}[6h]) by (route) -> 0.54
avg_over_time(kv_cache_hitrate{route=\"/chat/stream\"}[24h]) -> 0.72
rate(kv_cache_evictions_total{route=\"/chat/stream\"}[6h]) -> 0.021/s
sum(kv_cache_mem_bytes{route=\"/chat/stream\"}) -> 4.2e9
```

maria: quick profile notes: increased time in kernel_selector.choose() and an uptick on the kv_lookup mismatch path (more key hash comparisons). Measured L2/LLC miss increase ~+30% on lookup-heavy worker threads.

ingrid: can you paste sampling histograms for prefix_key length and reuse_by_route? Maybe prompt templates changed and increased prefix variance.

maria: prefix_length histogram (median): 12 -> 26 for /chat/stream in last 24h. reuse_by_route (sampled): top-10 routes show /chat/stream drop from 0.72 -> 0.55, others stable.

tyler: so two axes: prefix diversity increased (less reuse) and kernel-selector change altered key serialization or memory layout which increases probe cost -> more evictions under same pressure. Do we have evidence kernel affects serialization?

maria: hypothesis: `aten_v2` path changed tuple order when serializing prefix keys (minor field reorder). Most keys still match, but mixed clients (old vs new) lead to mismatch on reads written by different code paths. Also the new kernel's memory layout raises lookup cost slightly which surfaces under pressure.

sam: can we validate by running a canary with the old selector for this route only? A/B for 10-20% should be quick.

maria: started a 10% canary using old selector for /chat/stream at 1978642005. Early numbers (first 30m): canary hit-rate 71%, control 53%. Eviction rate on canary ~50% of control.

tyler: that lines up. Quick mitigation ideas: add a key-normalizer at write/read boundary so kernel path differences don't matter; small hotfix. Longer: prevent kernel path from owning serialization format or add invariants/tests.

maria: proposed plan:
- short-term: inject key-normalizer middleware in runtime read/write (patch + hotfix rollout)
- mid-term: per-route kernel-selector override and add serialization compatibility tests in infra CI
- observability: add `prefix_entropy` and `kvcache_reuse_delta` cards to console and alert when reuse drops >10%

ingrid: agree. Also please add a dashboard card: \"prefix entropy by route\" and \"kvcache reuse (6h vs 24h)\". Include trace links for examples.

perf-bot: deploybot: canary started kv-canary-197864 at 1978642005 by maria

maria: I'll open the hotfix PR tonight: one-line normalizer + unit tests. Will attach perf graphs and canary dashboard once I have 1h of data. cc @ingrid @sam @tyler

sam: nice work catching this quickly. If middleware patch looks low-risk we can hotfix during low traffic window.

maria: agreed — hotfix target: 02:00 UTC. PR: will post link here.

deploybot: status: kv-canary-197864 health=passing (latency OK)

maria: thanks everyone — will follow up with PR + final canary report.
